title: Universal Bounds On Entropy Production From Fluctuating Coarse-grained Trajectories
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This Review discusses universal lower bounds on entropy production inferred from coarse-grained trajectories in stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Entropy production is a key measure of non-equilibrium behavior but is difficult to measure directly in partially observed systems; model-free bounds are needed.
method: The Review surveys stochastic thermodynamics approaches that use coarse-grained observables (states, currents, correlations, waiting times) to derive lower bounds on entropy production.
result: Universal bounds on entropy production are obtained from fluctuating coarse-grained trajectories, applicable to both steady and time-dependent regimes.
conclusion: These bounds provide practical tools for estimating dissipation in complex systems where full microscopic information is unavailable.

title: A Hybrid Anyon-otto Thermal Machine
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum thermal machine using anyons, demonstrating enhanced performance due to non-Abelian statistics.
motivation: To explore the thermodynamic advantages of anyonic systems, which exhibit exotic exchange statistics, in quantum thermal machines.
method: The authors model an Otto cycle using anyons in a one-dimensional lattice, deriving expressions for work and efficiency based on braiding and fusion properties.
result: The anyonic Otto engine achieves higher efficiency and power output compared to conventional quantum engines, with performance linked to topological invariants.
conclusion: Anyonic systems offer a new platform for quantum thermodynamics, potentially enabling more efficient thermal machines through topological effects.

title: Thermodynamic Sampling Of Materials Using Neutral-atom Quantum Computers
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a thermodynamic sampling method for materials using neutral-atom quantum computers, leveraging quantum thermodynamics to efficiently explore configuration spaces.
motivation: Classical sampling of materials' configurational spaces is computationally expensive; quantum computers may offer advantages by exploiting thermodynamic principles.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that maps the material's energy landscape to a quantum system and uses neutral-atom quantum computers to perform thermodynamic sampling via quantum annealing or variational methods.
result: The method demonstrates improved sampling efficiency for certain materials compared to classical approaches, with potential for scaling to larger systems.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers can be effectively used for thermodynamic sampling of materials, opening new avenues for materials discovery and design.

title: Variational Gibbs State Preparation On Trapped-ion Devices
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: A variational quantum algorithm for preparing Gibbs states on trapped-ion devices, with experimental demonstration on IonQ Aria.
motivation: Gibbs state preparation is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are resource-intensive. A variational approach offers a more efficient alternative.
method: The authors propose a variational quantum algorithm that minimizes the free energy using a parameterized quantum circuit, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: The algorithm successfully prepares Gibbs states of small spin chains with high fidelity, and the experimental results match theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Variational Gibbs state preparation is feasible on current trapped-ion hardware, enabling studies of thermal states and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Photonic Qubit Gates Via 1d Scattering From An Array Of Two-level Emitters
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a photonic quantum gate using 1D scattering from an array of two-level emitters.
motivation: To realize high-fidelity quantum gates for photonic qubits, which are essential for quantum networks and computing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the scattering of single photons from a 1D array of two-level emitters, deriving the effective interaction and gate operation.
result: They show that the array can implement controlled-phase gates with high fidelity and low loss, leveraging collective effects.
conclusion: This approach offers a scalable and efficient way to implement photonic quantum gates using solid-state emitters.

title: Erbium-doped Fiber Quantum Memory For Chip-integrated Quantum-dot Single Photons At 980 Nm
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates an erbium-doped fiber quantum memory for chip-integrated quantum-dot single photons at 980 nm, achieving high efficiency and long storage time.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks, and integrating them with chip-based single-photon sources is a key step toward scalable architectures.
method: The authors use an erbium-doped fiber as a quantum memory, storing photons from a quantum dot source at 980 nm via atomic frequency comb protocol.
result: They achieve storage and retrieval of single photons with high fidelity and efficiency, demonstrating compatibility with integrated photonic platforms.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum memory for networking applications, particularly for chip-integrated systems.

title: Beyond Quantum Linear Optics With Adaptive Boson Sampling
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an adaptive boson sampling architecture that goes beyond linear optics by using measurement-based feedback to realize nonlinear optical evolutions.
motivation: Standard boson sampling relies on linear optical evolution, which is classically simulable in certain regimes; achieving nonlinearity is crucial for demonstrating quantum advantage and enabling new quantum information protocols.
method: The authors implement an adaptive boson sampling setup where measurement outcomes are used to dynamically adjust subsequent optical elements, effectively realizing nonlinear transformations through feedback.
result: They provide witnesses that certify the nonlinear-optical evolution, showing that the output distribution cannot be reproduced by any linear optical circuit.
conclusion: Adaptive boson sampling offers a path to nonlinear quantum optics with potential applications in quantum computing and simulation, though the current demonstration is proof-of-principle.

title: Generating Logical Magic States With The Aid Of non-Abelian Topological Order
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate logical magic states using non-Abelian topological order, specifically Fibonacci anyons, to enable universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computation, but their generation is challenging. Topological systems offer inherent fault tolerance, and non-Abelian anyons can provide a natural resource for magic states.
method: The authors design a protocol using Fibonacci anyons in a topological system to create logical magic states through braiding and measurement, leveraging the non-Abelian statistics.
result: They demonstrate that logical magic states can be generated with high fidelity using topological operations, potentially reducing the overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: Non-Abelian topological order provides a promising platform for generating magic states, advancing the feasibility of universal topological quantum computation.

title: Topological Phase Transitions And Mixed-state Order In A Hubbard Quantum Simulator
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 27 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports an experimental observation of a topological phase transition in a Hubbard quantum simulator using ultracold erbium atoms.
motivation: Topological phases are hard to distinguish with local measurements; the authors aim to reveal a transition between two such phases.
method: They use ultracold erbium atoms in an optical lattice to simulate the Hubbard model and probe the phase transition via local observables.
result: A transition between topological phases is observed, and it disappears when two systems are stacked or disorder information is lost.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a method to detect topological phase transitions in quantum simulators, relevant for condensed matter physics.

title: Phonon Focusing At Room Temperature
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 23 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates phonon focusing at room temperature, enabling directional heat control via crystal orientation.
motivation: Phonon focusing, previously observed only at low temperatures, could enable directional heat transport for thermal management technologies.
method: The authors experimentally measure heat flow in crystalline materials at room temperature, observing anisotropic phonon propagation.
result: Long-lived phonon waves and orientation-dependent heat transport are observed at room temperature.
conclusion: Room-temperature phonon focusing offers opportunities for directional heat control in future technologies.

title: A Magnetic Impurity Sets Off Ripples In A Kagome Superconductor
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic Kondo resonances in a magnetically doped kagome superconductor.
motivation: The role of magnetic impurities in shaping superconductivity and electronic order in kagome metals is not well understood.
method: The study uses scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy to probe the electronic structure of a magnetically doped kagome superconductor.
result: Anisotropic Kondo resonances intertwined with the superconducting gap are observed.
conclusion: The findings reveal new physics of magnetic impurities in kagome superconductors, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Capturing The First Moments After High-energy Molecular Impact
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 July 2026;
tldr: This paper uses attosecond X-ray free-electron laser to capture ultrafast electron dynamics after high-energy molecular impact.
motivation: Understanding the initial femtosecond-scale processes following high-energy particle collisions with molecules is crucial for chemistry and physics.
method: The study employs an attosecond X-ray free-electron laser to probe quantum mechanical motion of electrons in molecules immediately after impact.
result: The experiment successfully captured the first moments of electron dynamics, revealing how chemical bonds begin to break.
conclusion: Attosecond X-ray free-electron lasers enable direct observation of ultrafast electron motion, advancing our understanding of molecular dynamics.

title: From Electronic Clovers To Emergent Quantum Matter
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the emergence of charge order and superconductivity in cuprates from atomic-scale electronic states, using scanning tunneling microscopy.
motivation: Understanding how charge order and superconductivity emerge from the atomic scale in high-temperature superconductors is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) to image electronic states in hole-doped cuprates, tracking the evolution from atomic-scale clover-shaped states to larger motifs.
result: They observe that the first holes create atomic-scale electronic states that combine into larger patterns, providing a bottom-up view of charge order and superconducting phenomena.
conclusion: The work offers a microscopic picture of emergent quantum matter in cuprates, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Electron Orbitals Choose A Direction
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of surface 5d-orbital order in an intermetallic compound, revealed through electronic band structure and real-space fingerprints.
motivation: Orbital order is difficult to isolate because it often intertwines with lattice and magnetic transitions; this study aims to directly observe orbital order in a clean system.
method: The authors use experimental techniques to probe the electronic band structure and real-space signatures of a surface 5d-orbital order in an intermetallic compound.
result: They successfully isolate and characterize a surface 5d-orbital order, providing clear fingerprints in both momentum and real space.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a method to disentangle orbital order from other orders, advancing the understanding of electronic ordering phenomena.

title: Manipulating Spin Dynamics Via Exciton–exciton Interactions For Bright Spin Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 23 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates spin light-emitting diodes with high dissymmetry and long lifetime by manipulating spin dynamics via exciton–exciton interactions in hybrid chiral metal halide heterostructures.
motivation: To achieve bright spin light-emitting diodes that directly emit circularly polarized light, which is important for next-generation displays and spintronic devices.
method: The authors use exciton–exciton interactions in hybrid chiral metal halide heterostructures to suppress spin relaxation, enabling efficient spin injection and radiative recombination.
result: They achieve a dissymmetry factor of 0.2 and a half-lifetime of 5,000 hours at an initial luminance of 100 cd m−2.
conclusion: Exciton–exciton interactions can effectively control spin dynamics, leading to practical spin LEDs with high performance and stability.

title: Real-time Optical Signal Equalization With A Silicon Photonic Spatially Distributed Reservoir Computer
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of real-time optical signal equalization using a silicon photonic reservoir computer.
motivation: To mitigate fiber distortions in high-speed optical communication using a compact, low-power photonic chip.
method: A silicon photonic spatially distributed reservoir computer processes a 28-Gbps on-off keying signal in real time.
result: Bit error rates as low as 4 × 10^-7 are achieved.
conclusion: Photonic reservoir computing is a viable approach for real-time equalization in optical communication links.

title: Emergence Of Fermi-liquid And Bcs Physics In Overdoped Cuprates
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 16 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that observed behaviors in overdoped cuprates can be explained by substitutional disorder in a d-wave superconductor, rather than requiring non-Fermi-liquid physics.
motivation: To resolve the apparent inconsistency between weak-coupling Fermi-liquid theory and experimental observations in overdoped cuprates.
method: The authors present a perspective based on theoretical arguments and analysis of substitutional disorder effects in a short-correlation-length d-wave superconductor.
result: They propose that in the disorder-free limit, a weak-coupling Fermi-liquid-based BCS description is possible.
conclusion: Substitutional disorder is key to understanding overdoped cuprate behavior, and disorder-free systems may align with conventional theory.

title: Data-driven Reduced Modeling Of Neural Dynamics
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper uses data-driven methods to find invariant slow manifolds in recurrent neural networks, reducing their dynamics to low-dimensional models for decision-making and working-memory tasks.
motivation: Recurrent neural networks are high-dimensional and hard to interpret; reducing them to low-dimensional models can reveal core dynamics and improve understanding of neural computations.
method: The authors apply a data-driven approach to identify invariant slow manifolds from neural activity data, constructing reduced-order models that capture essential dynamics.
result: They uncover robust low-dimensional structures underlying decision-making and working-memory tasks, and the reduced models make testable predictions about neural computations.
conclusion: Data-driven reduced modeling is effective for extracting interpretable dynamics from recurrent neural networks, with potential applications in neuroscience.

title: Experimental Implementation Of A Discrete-time Quantum Walk On Biological Networks
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 July 2026;
tldr: This paper experimentally implements a discrete-time quantum walk on biological networks, demonstrating quantum dynamics on graph structures derived from biological data.
motivation: To explore quantum walks on complex biological networks, which may reveal quantum effects in biological systems or provide new computational tools.
method: A discrete-time quantum walk is implemented on a photonic platform, with the walker's evolution defined by the adjacency structure of biological networks.
result: The experimental implementation successfully shows quantum interference and probability distributions characteristic of quantum walks on non-regular graphs.
conclusion: Quantum walks can be realized on biological network topologies, but the work is primarily an experimental demonstration without direct connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Universities Need Transparent Quantum Hardware
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that universities should procure transparent quantum hardware for educational purposes rather than relying solely on cloud access.
motivation: The authors believe that students need hands-on experience with quantum hardware to understand the gap between ideal circuits and physical measurements.
method: The paper presents a perspective based on educational needs and the limitations of cloud-based quantum computing access.
result: It advocates for universities to invest in teachable quantum systems that allow students to see and interact with the hardware.
conclusion: Universities should prioritize educational transparency in quantum hardware procurement to enhance learning outcomes.

title: The Importance Of Imagery In Quantum Mechanics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 July 2026;
tldr: A historical reflection on the role of visualization and imagery in the conceptual development of quantum mechanics.
motivation: To explore the philosophical and historical debate between Heisenberg and Schrödinger regarding the necessity of visualizable models in quantum theory.
method: Historical analysis and philosophical discussion based on the author's expertise.
result: The paper argues that imagery has played a crucial but often underappreciated role in shaping quantum mechanics.
conclusion: Visualization remains a subtle and important aspect of quantum theory, despite its abstract mathematical formulation.

title: Graphene Fet Microfluidic Platform For Electrochemical Molecular Fingerprinting
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a graphene FET microfluidic platform for electrochemical molecular fingerprinting.
motivation: To integrate graphene-FET based microfluidic modules into a single experimental workflow for molecular analysis.
method: The platform combines graphene field-effect transistors with microfluidics to enable electrochemical sensing.
result: The platform achieves electrochemical molecular fingerprinting, but no specific performance metrics are provided in the abstract.
conclusion: The platform offers a new integrated approach for molecular analysis using graphene FETs and microfluidics.

title: Dynamics Of Supracellular Keratin Bundling And Nuclear Uncaging In Stretched Epithelia
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 27 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the mechanical response of epithelial cells under stretch, focusing on keratin filament bundling and nuclear uncaging.
motivation: Understanding how cells protect the nucleus from mechanical stress is important for cell biology and tissue mechanics.
method: The authors apply large deformations to epithelial tissues and observe keratin filament bundling and nuclear release using microscopy and mechanical measurements.
result: Under large deformations, intermediate filaments bundle and ultimately release the nucleus from its cage.
conclusion: The study reveals a mechanism for nuclear protection under extreme mechanical stress.

title: Observation Of Superconductivity-induced Leading-edge Gap In A Bilayer Nickelate
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of a superconducting gap in bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7.
motivation: To understand the superconducting mechanism in nickelates, which are a new class of high-temperature superconductors.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic structure and superconducting gap.
result: A leading-edge gap was observed, and the Fermi surface was found to derive mainly from the d_z^2 band.
conclusion: The results provide direct evidence of superconductivity-induced gap in bilayer nickelates, confirming their unconventional superconductivity.

title: Enhanced Inverse Compton Scattering Via Spontaneous Focusing Induced By A Coated Plasma Mirror
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 23 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates enhanced inverse Compton scattering efficiency using a coated plasma mirror to focus laser pulses, achieving 10^-3 efficiency and photon energies up to hundreds of MeV.
motivation: Inverse Compton scattering is a key mechanism for generating high-energy photons, but its efficiency is typically low. Enhancing efficiency could enable compact, high-brightness gamma-ray sources.
method: The authors propose and experimentally demonstrate a coated plasma mirror that spontaneously focuses the reflected laser pulse, increasing the local intensity and thus the scattering efficiency.
result: They achieve an inverse Compton scattering efficiency of 10^-3 with photon energies extending to hundreds of megaelectronvolts using a 400 TW laser.
conclusion: Coated plasma mirrors provide a practical way to enhance inverse Compton scattering, potentially enabling compact high-energy photon sources for applications in nuclear physics, medicine, and materials science.

abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents circularly polarized organic light-emitting diodes with integrated memory and computing for 3D displays.

method: The authors use an adaptive laser-tagging technique in an optofluidic microcavity, leveraging thermal phonon transfer and dynamic resonance tracking to achieve spectrometry-based detection.
result: The sensor achieves high sensitivity, low noise, and effective selectivity for hydrogen detection over a nine-decade concentration span.
conclusion: The proposed method enables precise hydrogen concentration detection with broad dynamic range, suitable for practical sensing applications.

title: Was Schrödinger Ever A Determinist?
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This paper examines Schrödinger's philosophical views on determinism, arguing that he was not a strict determinist but held a nuanced position.
motivation: To correct the common portrayal of Schrödinger as a reactionary determinist and to clarify his actual philosophical stance on determinism in quantum mechanics.
method: Historical and philosophical analysis of Schrödinger's writings and correspondence, contextualizing his views within the broader debate on determinism.
result: Schrödinger's position on determinism was complex and evolved; he rejected both naive determinism and indeterminism, advocating for a form of 'statistical determinism'.
conclusion: Schrödinger should not be labeled a determinist; his views were more radical and nuanced, contributing to foundational discussions in quantum mechanics.

title: Tailoring d–p Orbital Hybridization Of Single-atom Cu-N2S Sites For Enhanced photo-Fenton Reaction
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports a Cu-N2S single-atom catalyst for photo-Fenton degradation of pollutants, focusing on d-p orbital hybridization to enhance H2O2 activation.
motivation: To develop efficient and pH-robust catalysts for pollutant degradation via photo-Fenton reaction.
method: Synthesized asymmetric Cu-N2S coordination sites and characterized their electronic structure using X-ray absorption spectroscopy and DFT calculations.
result: The Cu-N2S catalyst exhibits high photo-Fenton activity over a broad pH range due to enhanced d-p hybridization and an anti-band-center effect.
conclusion: Asymmetric coordination engineering is an effective strategy to boost catalytic performance in photo-Fenton reactions.

title: Skeletal Muscle Properties In Long Covid And Me/cfs Differ From Those Induced By Bed Rest
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies skeletal muscle properties in long COVID and ME/CFS patients, finding distinct changes not explained by physical inactivity.
motivation: To determine whether reduced aerobic capacity in long COVID and ME/CFS is solely due to physical inactivity or involves specific skeletal muscle pathology.
method: Comparison of skeletal muscle biopsies and functional measurements from long COVID, ME/CFS, and bed rest control groups.
result: Long COVID and ME/CFS patients exhibit distinct skeletal muscle changes that differ from those induced by bed rest alone.
conclusion: Skeletal muscle abnormalities in long COVID and ME/CFS are not solely attributable to physical inactivity, suggesting other pathophysiological mechanisms.

title: Iron Deficiency Strategy Toward Single-phase High-entropy M-type Ferrites For Broadband Millimeter-wave Absorption With Low Thickness
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026;

method: An iron deficiency strategy was used to synthesize single-phase high-entropy M-type ferrites.
result: A broad millimeter-wave absorption bandwidth of 12.18 GHz around 35 GHz with thickness below 1 mm was achieved.
conclusion: The iron deficiency strategy is effective for producing high-entropy ferrites with excellent millimeter-wave absorption properties.

abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper investigates the atomic-scale mechanism of ammonia inhibition during NOx SCR on Cu-CHA catalysts, a topic in catalysis chemistry.
motivation: Understanding ammonia inhibition is crucial for improving the efficiency of NOx reduction in lean-burn engines.
method: The authors use experimental and computational methods to clarify the inhibition mechanism at the atomic scale.
result: They identify the specific atomic-scale processes responsible for ammonia inhibition.
conclusion: The findings provide insights for designing better SCR catalysts with reduced inhibition.

title: Food-related Energy Consumption Can Help Reveal Poverty In Rural Chinese Households
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 July 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces an Energy Engel Coefficient using food-related energy consumption to identify poverty in rural China, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: Traditional income-based poverty measures may miss low-income households; the authors propose a novel indicator based on energy consumption patterns.
method: Using household survey data from China, they calculate the Energy Engel Coefficient and compare it with income-based poverty identification.
result: The Energy Engel Coefficient identifies low-income rural households not captured by traditional income measures.
conclusion: Food-related energy consumption can serve as an alternative poverty indicator in rural China.

title: Enantioselective Synthesis Of Ring-constrained Biaryls Via A Twist-expand-seal Strategy
